products.name: Microsoft Purview — DLP, Sensitivity Labels & Retention (Government / GCC High) — Commercial
products.short_description: The Government (GCC High) edition of the Purview DLP, labels & retention solution — US-sovereign-cloud portals/endpoints and Commercial-vs-GCC-High parity gaps called out. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Roll out Purview DLP, labels & retention correctly on a GCC High tenant

Microsoft Purview in GCC High is not the Commercial portal with a different login — admin URLs differ (compliance.microsoft.us / security.microsoft.us), and several Purview capabilities lag, are limited, or are absent versus Commercial. This is the Government edition: DLP, sensitivity labels, and retention authored for the US sovereign cloud, with the GCC High portals, endpoints, and parity gaps called out so a government tenant is configured correctly — not with Commercial steps that silently fail.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — the Purview information-protection model (sensitivity labels + label policies + auto-labeling, DLP across M365/endpoints, retention labels/policies and records management), and how they work together.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Microsoft 365 + Purview licensing, Entra ID, a label taxonomy, data owners, a pilot scope, change control) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: design the label taxonomy, publish labels and label policies, configure auto-labeling, build DLP policies in audit and tune, set retention labels/policies and records, pilot, validate, then expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — Purview configuration discovery, label/DLP/retention coverage validation, a classification + DLP-event report, safe remediation of gaps, and a protection-scope group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Purview DLP, labels, and retention deployed correctly on GCC High — right portals, right endpoints, parity gaps handled — proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • PURVIEWG-Discovery.ps1 — inventory Purview labels, DLP, and retention on a GCC High tenant (read-only)
    • PURVIEWG-Remediation.ps1 — safely remediate detected Purview gaps on a GCC High tenant (defaults to -WhatIf)
    • PURVIEWG-Report.ps1 — produce a Purview coverage / classification / DLP-event report (read-only, GCC High)
    • PURVIEWG-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — build/adjust the Purview protection-scope group for staged expansion (defaults to -WhatIf)
    • PURVIEWG-Validation.ps1 — validate that the designed Purview objects exist and are scoped (read-only, GCC High)

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
